themes_detail.label: Dead and dying trees spike
themes_detail.summary: Sunset Park residents filed 9 complaints about dead or dying trees THIS WEEK, a 620% spike above the 1.2-per-week average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.24), signaling either a rapid environmental deterioration or sudden storm damage requiring urgent investigation and remediation.
evidence: 9 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (620% increase, z-score: 5.24)
Concurrent spike in overgrown tree/branches complaints: 9 complaints last week vs. 1.4 weekly average (554% increase)
Concurrent spike in illegal tree damage complaints: 9 complaints last week vs. 1.6 weekly average (454% increase)
CB budget requests show longstanding park/green space expansion requests, suggesting prior underinvestment in tree maintenance
reporting_angles: Was there a recent storm, pest outbreak, or disease affecting Sunset Park's urban forest?
Are Parks Department inspections and tree-trimming budgets keeping pace with deterioration, or is this a deferred maintenance crisis?

themes_detail.label: Drug activity explodes
themes_detail.summary: Sunset Park saw 5 drug activity complaints last week, a 1900% spike from a near-zero 0.2-per-week baseline over 8 weeks (z-score: 10.97), representing the most severe statistical anomaly in the dataset and demanding urgent public safety investigation.
evidence: 5 drug activity complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1900% increase, z-score: 10.97, highest severity)
This represents an unprecedented spike in a previously quiet indicator
CB budget requests include expanded street outreach from Department of Homeless Services, suggesting prior concerns about street-level conditions
reporting_angles: Is this spike concentrated in specific blocks or neighborhoods within Sunset Park? Map it.
What changed last week—new dealers, supply chain shift, reduced enforcement, or housing instability among vulnerable populations?
Are NYPD and local outreach organizations aware? What resources do they need?

themes_detail.label: Boiler complaints triple
themes_detail.summary: Three boiler complaints filed THIS WEEK, a 500% spike from a 0.5-per-week baseline over 8 weeks (z-score: 5.0), occurring amid a season of heat/hot water complaints (1,028 over 90 days) and suggesting potential systemic heating failures in older residential buildings.
evidence: 3 boiler complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (500% increase, z-score: 5.0)
Heat/hot water is the #2 complaint category overall in CD 307 with 1,028 complaints over 90 days, indicating chronic housing condition issues
Boiler spike coincides with seasonal heating demand and may reflect deferred maintenance or aging infrastructure
reporting_angles: Are these failures concentrated in older public housing or private buildings? NYCHA vs. private landlord breakdown?
What's the typical response time from HPD for boiler violations, and are landlords getting cited?
Interview affected residents about cold apartments and health impacts on families, elderly, children.

themes_detail.label: General 311 complaint surge
themes_detail.summary: General 311 complaints jumped to 15 THIS WEEK, a 167% spike above the 5.6-per-week baseline over 8 weeks (z-score: 3.91), suggesting residents are escalating unclassified or multi-issue complaints, potentially masking specific emerging problems.
evidence: 15 general complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (167% increase, z-score: 3.91)
Occurs alongside multiple other spikes (drug activity, trees, boilers), suggesting residents may be filing catch-all complaints when issues don't fit standard categories
May indicate frustration with 311 system responsiveness or unmet needs not captured by existing complaint types
reporting_angles: What are residents actually complaining about under 'general'? FOIA the text of these 15 complaints.
Is the 311 system failing to categorize emerging issues, or are residents circumventing slow category-specific processes?

themes_detail.label: Unleashed dog complaints 3 weeks ago
themes_detail.summary: Three unleashed dog complaints filed 3 weeks ago, a 2300% spike from a 0.1-per-week baseline over 8 weeks (z-score: 8.69), though the spike appears to have subsided; worth monitoring for resurgence given severity but lower priority than current-week signals.
evidence: 3 unleashed dog complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2300% increase, z-score: 8.69)
Spike has subsided in most recent weeks, suggesting either isolated incident or temporary enforcement gap
May correlate with neighborhood dog parks or off-leash areas; timing suggests possible seasonal pattern
reporting_angles: Was there a specific unleashed dog incident or pack problem 3 weeks ago, or is this a chronic leash law enforcement issue?
Has the problem returned, or did it resolve naturally?
